issue.title: Epic landing leaves its own Justfile --epic-symbol entries behind, so the next agent's just check is the thing that discovers them
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY: closed task sase-o4 (2026-08-17), whose second RELATED note observed the pattern and explicitly recorded that the specific instance being fixed there did not address it. Routed to its own task by the backlog-triage agent rather than dying with that bead.

THE PATTERN, MEASURED: 'sase bead search' over task beads finds SEVEN separate cleanup tasks for the identical failure, all closed, spanning about two months and accelerating:
  sase-by / sase-bz  - closed bead sase-bj.3
  sase-i0            - closed bead sase-hq
  sase-jg            - closed bead sase-j3
  sase-kc            - closed bead sase-js
  sase-nm            - closed bead sase-n9
  sase-o4            - closed bead sase-nb
Four of those seven (sase-jg, sase-kc, sase-nm, sase-o4) landed within the last week.

MECHANISM: Symvision's epic whitelist lets an in-progress epic pass '--epic-symbol "<bead>(<symbol>)"' in the Justfile's _lint-symvision recipe to exempt a symbol that is not yet wired up. The exemption is keyed to the bead, and Symvision correctly rejects an entry whose bead is closed: "bead '<id>' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol." So the gate already detects the condition. What is missing is that nothing does the cleanup at the moment the epic closes. The entries go stale the instant 'sase bead close <epic>' succeeds, and the discovery mechanism is that some unrelated agent's mandatory 'just check' goes red on a clean master tree it did not touch.

COST PER INSTANCE: every agent whose tree reaches the lint gate between the epic's close and the cleanup landing gets a red 'just check' with no relationship to its own diff. sase-o4's reporter confirmed with 'git stash -u' that master itself was red. Each instance then costs a triage sweep, a filed task bead, a TaskTriage gate for the owner, and a worker launch - for cleanup the closing agent was best placed to do, since it is the one that knows why each symbol was exempted.

WHY THE CLOSING AGENT IS THE RIGHT OWNER: the land prompt already tells the land agent to run 'just symvision' AFTER closing the epic, because epic-symbol whitelist entries expire at close, and to remove the stale entries and unused code it reports. That instruction exists and is still being missed often enough to produce four beads in a week, so an instruction alone is not sufficient - the step needs to be discoverable and hard to skip.

SCOPE: make the epic close reliably retire its own whitelist entries rather than leaving them for the next agent. Candidate approaches, to be chosen by the worker:
  (a) give the land step a real command that lists the closing epic's own --epic-symbol entries, so the agent does not have to grep the Justfile and reason about which of the entries are its own (sase-o4's fix had to leave the still-open sase-n4 and sase-n4.5 entries untouched while removing five sase-nb ones);
  (b) have 'sase bead close' on an epic detect remaining entries keyed to that bead and refuse, warn, or emit the exact follow-up work;
  (c) tighten the land xprompt so the symvision pass is a gate rather than a trailing instruction.
Note that the per-symbol resolution is genuine judgment work and must NOT be automated away: sase-o4's precedent resolved its five symbols three different ways (tools/ pragma for two, privatize-and-drop-from-__all__ for two, outright delete plus move the seam into tests/_conftest_runtime.py for one), per the Symvision epic-whitelist policy in sase/memory/symvision.md. The goal is to make the work happen at close time, not to make it mechanical.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the epic-whitelist policy itself, and the separate transient-lookup defect in closed task sase-it (Symvision briefly failing to find an existing in-progress bead), which is a different failure with a different cause.

VERIFICATION: after the change, closing an epic that still has --epic-symbol entries should surface them at close time. A regression test should cover the discovery path; reproducing the human-judgment cleanup is not required.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-o4 — the seventh and most recent instance of this pattern, and the bead that proposed this systemic fix. Its close note records the full resolution shape for its five sase-nb symbols and is the best worked example of what the close-time step has to produce.

RELATED: sase-nm, sase-kc, sase-jg, sase-i0, sase-bz, sase-by — the six earlier instances, all closed. Read a couple before designing the fix: they show the entries are always removed correctly once someone looks, so the defect is purely one of WHEN the cleanup happens, not of how hard it is.

RELATED: sase-it — closed task for a Symvision epic-symbol bead LOOKUP that transiently missed an existing in-progress bead. Same Justfile mechanism, opposite direction (a live bead reported as missing, rather than a closed bead's entry left behind). Keep the two separate; do not let a fix here reintroduce that flake.

RELATED: sase-mk — in-progress bead for a different standing symvision red on master (private ACE provider-routing symbols imported by non-test files). Not a duplicate: that one is about symbol visibility, this one is about whitelist lifecycle. Named because a worker here will be reading the same _lint-symvision recipe.

evidence.note: Eighth instance, and the first observed mid-epic rather than post-land: on HEAD 7202e847b with a tests-only diff (tests/monitor/*.py), just check fails at lint (symvision) on 5 entries keyed to CLOSED PHASE beads of the STILL IN-PROGRESS epic sase-o8 — sase-o8.3(RankedPlaceholder), sase-o8.3(build_placeholder_ranking_context), sase-o8.3(rank_common_placeholders), sase-o8.3(rank_recent_common_placeholders) (Justfile:326-329) and sase-o8.4(load_common_placeholder_index) (Justfile:330). Reproduce: just install && just _lint-symvision. This widens the scope recorded in this bead: entries go stale at PHASE close, not only at epic close, so a fix that only hooks 'sase bead close <epic>' would still have left this tree red — phases 3 and 4 closed while phase 5 (sase-o8.5) is open. Impact confirmed as before: an agent with an unrelated diff eats the red gate. DISCOVERED ISSUE note also recorded on sase-o8 for its land agent.

Independent reproduction on 2026-08-17 while implementing monitor_node_under_starter. just check died at lint (symvision) after every earlier gate passed (fmt, ruff, mypy, flags, pyscripts, changelog, patch/stitch). Symvision rejects five Justfile _lint-symvision entries whose phase beads are closed while parent epic sase-o8 is still in_progress: sase-o8.3(RankedPlaceholder), sase-o8.3(build_placeholder_ranking_context), sase-o8.3(rank_common_placeholders), sase-o8.3(rank_recent_common_placeholders), and sase-o8.4(load_common_placeholder_index). This tree does not touch Justfile or those symbols. Same mid-epic leftover already recorded on sase-o7 and as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on sase-o8.

Independent reproduction 2026-08-17 while implementing bead_work_family_member_bead_association (unrelated tree; no Justfile edits). just check died at lint (symvision) after fmt/ruff/mypy/flags/pyscripts/changelog/terminology passed: Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-o8.4(PlaceholderRankingMetadata)': bead 'sase-o8.4' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol. Same mid-epic leftover: phase sase-o8.4 is closed while sase-o8.5 and the parent epic are still in_progress. This names PlaceholderRankingMetadata specifically; earlier +1s cited sase-o8.4(load_common_placeholder_index) and the o8.3 ranking symbols.

Independent reproduction on 2026-08-17 from the sase-o9 land agent, on a clean master (26fefdab7) whose working tree is empty. 'just symvision' dies before scanning: "Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-o8.4(PlaceholderRankingMetadata)': bead 'sase-o8.4' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol." So 'just check' and 'just check-full' are red repo-wide for every agent again, and this landing had to re-run symvision by hand with that one entry dropped to get any signal on its own symbols (clean — sase-o9 introduced no unused public symbols and left no whitelist entries of its own; sase-o9.2 removed its own sase-o9.2(monitor_row_agent_name) entry when the symbol gained a real consumer).

NEW DATA POINT FOR THE MECHANISM: this is the second distinct instance from the SAME epic within about an hour — sase-o8.2's pair was reported earlier by 04j, and now sase-o8.4's entry has surfaced. sase-o8's phases all closed at 13:07Z and its land agent (sase-o8.land) is still QUEUED for a runner slot, so the window between 'phase closes' and 'land agent gets scheduled' is itself a red-master window, independent of whether the land agent eventually does the cleanup correctly. Any fix that only hardens the land step will still leave this window open; consider whether the phase close, not just the epic close, should surface entries keyed to the closing bead.

payload.entry: FOLLOW-UP: just check-full (monitor 8kh80tpm9f9r) passed lint and 31998 tests; the only failure was the standing suite-cost gate. Corroborated on in-progress task sase-j0 with file:explicit:f1f7af7283734f11589594cf. Not caused by this leftover-discovery change.

Verified close-time leftover --epic-symbol discovery. sase bead close now refuses while Justfile --epic-symbol entries remain for the closing bead or its descendant suffixes; already-closed no-ops skip the check and --force does not bypass it. sase bead epic-symbols lists the working-tree entries (optionally scoped to one bead/descendants) in compact and JSON. Land and phase xprompts require that cleanup before close, and the ACE Beads close path uses the same refusal. Regression tests cover parse (quoted/bare/= flags), list (scoped/empty/json/fast-path), and close (phase leftover, epic descendant, sibling ignore, post-cleanup success, reclose skip, force still refuses). just check-full (monitor 8kh80tpm9f9r) passed every lint gate and 31998 tests; the only failure was the standing suite-cost gate, corroborated on in-progress sase-j0 (file:explicit:f1f7af7283734f11589594cf). Live smoke: sase bead epic-symbols sase-o7 prints no entries, so this close is allowed. Did not file a new task for PlaceholderRankingMetadata; 5abf9eb64 wired it and dropped the whitelist entry before this commit rebased.

evidence.note:
REPRODUCED AFTER THE FIX. On master HEAD 30077550b (2026-08-17), `just check` is red at lint (symvision) on a tree that touches only src/sase/ace/tui/proc_observer.py and two test files:
  Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-oc.8(set_completion_summary)': bead 'sase-oc.8' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol.

WHY THIS IS POST-CLOSE EVIDENCE, NOT AN OLD INSTANCE: `git merge-base --is-ancestor fa1948437 017b488e6` succeeds — sase-oc.8's own landing commit contains this bead's fix ('feat(bead): refuse close while leftover --epic-symbol entries remain', 2026-08-17 10:02 EDT). sase-oc.8 nonetheless closed at 2026-08-17T19:37:29Z, 5.5h later, with its entry still in the Justfile. `sase bead epic-symbols` (this bead's other deliverable) does exist in the tree and lists the leftover, so the listing half works and the refusal half did not fire.

TWO EXPLANATIONS NOT DISTINGUISHED HERE, both worth a look before deciding whether this bead's fix is complete:
  (a) the phase was closed through a path the refusal does not cover (the close-time check is documented as covering `sase bead close` and the ACE Beads close path);
  (b) the worker ran from an ephemeral sase_<N> workspace whose venv still had a pre-fa1948437 `sase` installed, so its own binary had no refusal — which would make the refusal only as reliable as each workspace's last `just install`.

IMPACT UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL REPORT: every agent whose tree reaches the lint gate is red for a diff it did not write. Also recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on in-progress epic sase-oc, whose land agent owns the cleanup.

PHASE-LEVEL VARIANT OF THE SAME GAP, REPRODUCED TODAY: the whitelist can also go stale mid-epic, not just at epic landing. Epic sase-p2 is still IN_PROGRESS, but its phase bead sase-p2.2 closed at 2026-08-18T00:45:45Z, and its six Justfile --epic-symbol entries (lines 336-341: EditorRepoMentionCatalog, EditorRepoMentionCatalogResult, RepoMentionSpan, editor_repo_mention_catalog_for_project, lookup_repo_mention, scan_repo_mentions) are keyed to that phase bead. `just check` on an unrelated diff (splitting src/sase/completion/candidates/catalog.py) passed every earlier gate and failed lint (symvision) with six 'bead sase-p2.2 is closed' errors.

IMPACT DETAIL THIS INSTANCE ADDS: here the exemptions are still substantively correct -- the consuming phase sase-p2.3 is in progress, and re-running symvision with only those six entries removed reports exactly those six symbols as unused public defs. So the cleanup a triaged worker would perform is a retarget (point the entries at sase-p2.3 or the epic), not a delete, and no land agent has even run yet for this epic. Any fix that only hooks the epic-close/land step would miss this case; the trigger is 'the bead named by an entry closed', which happens at every phase close too. DISCOVERED ISSUE recorded on epic sase-p2.

INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION, AND A SCOPE EXTENSION: the same stale-whitelist failure fires at PHASE close, not just epic close, so every fix candidate in this bead's SCOPE section (all three are keyed to 'sase bead close <epic>') would have missed this instance entirely.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-18, clean master fd2d71afc, no local diff): 'just check-full' passed fmt python/markdown, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, feature flags, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, and patch/stitch terminology, then failed lint (symvision) with six errors, aborting the recipe at Justfile line 680 before the remaining six gates (toobig, SASE validation, core-floor probe, committed plans, test cost, flake baseline) ever ran:
  sase-p3.11(RequiredPluginError), sase-p3.11(fail_closed_required_plugins),
  sase-p4.3(active_epic_resume), sase-p4.3(build_epic_resume_argv),
  sase-p4.3(epic_resume_origin_from_gate_source), sase-p4.3(submit_epic_resume_task).

WHY THIS IS THE PHASE VARIANT: sase-p3.11 and sase-p4.3 are PHASE beads, closed at 2026-08-18T03:01:08Z and 03:01:48Z. Their parent epics sase-p3 and sase-p4 are both still IN_PROGRESS with open phases (sase-p3.6-.10, .12-.14; sase-p4.4, .5), so no epic close has happened or will happen for hours. The exemptions are still legitimately needed -- I confirmed all six symbols remain unconsumed outside their defining module (src/sase/plugins/required.py, src/sase/bead/epic_resume_launch.py, each referenced only in-file and in __all__), and the open later phases are their intended consumers (sase-p4.4 'The epic_resume chop' clearly consumes the epic_resume_launch four). So the correct remediation here is NOT deletion but a re-key to the still-open later bead, which is a different action than the epic-close cleanup this bead currently describes.

TIMING EVIDENCE THAT THE GATE IS THE ONLY DISCOVERY MECHANISM: my own 'just check' on this same tree passed symvision fully green roughly two minutes before the two phase beads closed; the very next run went red with zero change to the tree. The reporter (sase-p2.land) had no relationship to either epic.

IMPACT, AS THIS BEAD PREDICTS: master's lint gate is red for every agent right now, and because symvision sits at line 680 of check-full, it also masks the six later gates -- an agent landing real work gets an unrelated red and an incomplete verification run.

SUGGESTED SCOPE WIDENING: whatever mechanism is chosen, key it to ANY bead close that leaves entries behind (phase or epic), and make the re-key-to-an-open-later-bead path first-class, since a mid-epic phase close usually still needs the exemption. 'sase bead epic-symbols <bead>' already exists and lists a bead's own entries; it appears not to be consulted at phase close.

I did not modify the Justfile: the correct re-key target is a judgment owned by the sase-p3 and sase-p4 land agents, and I recorded DISCOVERED ISSUE notes on both epics.

Independent reproduction while landing epic sase-p8 (2026-08-18, master c033ca4c4 + landing tree). NEW VARIANT — a PHASE close, not an epic close, also strands entries: 'just symvision' failed with "--epic-symbol 'sase-p1.7(GlossaryPanel)': bead 'sase-p1.7' is closed" while its parent epic sase-p1 and sibling phase sase-p1.8 are still IN_PROGRESS. So the window this bead describes is wider than 'sase bead close <epic>': every phase close opens it too, and the phase agent is not prompted to run symvision the way the land agent is. 'sase bead epic-symbols <phase>' does resolve the phase's own entry, so the data needed to gate 'sase bead close' on a phase already exists. FOURTH instance inside a single epic: sase-p8's phase agents separately hit stale entries for closed sase-p1.2, sase-p2.2, and sase-p3.11+sase-p4.3 within about three hours of each other. Unblocked the current tree by re-keying the row to the still-open parent sase-p1.

Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol. Phase sase-pq.3 closed at 2026-08-18T14:40:41Z claiming the Justfile dropped the entry and sase bead epic-symbols sase-pq.3 reported no leftovers, but this workspace HEAD 4cca5f2ce (the commit that added the exemption) still has --epic-symbol sase-pq.3(gate_chip_from_action_data) at Justfile:342. The parent epic sase-pq is still IN_PROGRESS with open phases .4-.7, and gate_chip_from_action_data still has no non-test consumer outside presentation.py. Same mid-epic leftover: a closed phase bead, a live exemption, every unrelated just check red. Scoped tests (1744) passed; I did not touch the Justfile.

Independent reproduction 2026-08-18 while implementing settled_monitor_gear_chip (docs/ace.md, docs/monitors.md, src/sase/monitor_state.py, src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_family_members.py, src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/_agent_list_*.py, src/sase/ace/tui/modals/help_modal/agents_bindings.py, and their tests — no Justfile edits). just check passed fmt/ruff/mypy/flags/pyscripts/test-waits/changelog/patch-stitch-terminology, then failed lint (symvision): Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-pq.3(gate_chip_from_action_data)': bead 'sase-pq.3' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol. Same instance already reported by 05z.f0.f0 at 2026-08-18T14:59:32Z; corroborating with a second independent reproduction from a different tree. gate_chip_from_action_data (src/sase/notification_gates/presentation.py:171) still has only a test consumer (tests/test_notification_gate_presentation.py) — no non-test caller anywhere in src/ or tests/ as of my checkout.
